read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for "PanLex 2024 exact same-meaning Hebrew-English lexical expression" (M21): 28,439 routes (axis: routes), 9,861 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 28,439 of the routes. The source audit: each route's store record names one row of the Hebrew table and one row of the English table of the lane's copy of the source (cointegrated/panlex-meanings at commit 0422f0e60f39, a curator's rearrangement of PanLex's database dump 20240301, in ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/panlex-hebrew-english-2026-07-14/). The English row's column txt equals the record's text on 28,439 of 28,439 records (axis: records), and the column meaning of the English row and of the Hebrew row equals the meaning id the record cites on 28,439 and on 28,439 of them; the record's two other text fields are empty on all of them. So a route comes from one field, the text of one expression on one meaning, and no test here stands on a guess about a field; the audit is evidence about the source and no part of any test. The source's own key to its signs: none found. The lane holds 26 files of the curator's and of PanLex's own pages (the curator's README, which names the columns and says only that txt is the full text of the expression; the manifests and the licence page in that folder; the publisher's pages under corpus-lane-builds/moses-works-own-stamp-v1/strand-3-the-publishers/fetch/), and none holds a word that names a sign: the search and its word list are the script builder/05-key-search.mjs and its output source-audit/key-search.json. The menu of the publisher's development site, on file, names a page called Text standardization whose body is not on file; fetching it needs the owner's word and was not done. So every shape's meaning here begins "unverified:".

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one Unicode code point (every route holds only characters of 16 bits, so a code point is one index of the JavaScript string). A letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}), of any script and in either case. A digit is one of 0 to 9, and no test asks for any other number character. A space is the character U+0020 only, and no test uses whitespace of any other kind. The letters A to Z are the 26 uppercase Latin letters and no others. Nothing is trimmed: the text is the whole route text as it stands, which is the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def; the text before and the text after the mark are the template's c.before and c.after, and what a bracket holds is the template's c.group, the same for an opener and for its closer. Directly before and directly after name the one character next to the mark or next to the named string; where the mark or the string stands at that end of the text no character stands there, so a test that asks for a character there fails, and a test that says if there is one passes. The whole text, exactly, means that the text equals the named string character for character. Ends in means that the last characters of the named thing are exactly the string. The word round the mark means three runs put together, with nothing between them: the run of letters that ends directly before the mark, taken back to the first character that is not a letter or to the start of the text; the mark itself; and the run of letters that begins directly after the mark, taken on to the first character that is not a letter or to the end of the text; either run of letters may be empty. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it, and a full stop after » belongs to the sentence and not to the string. Every string and every list minds case and is matched exact to the character, so «s» is the lowercase letter. No test uses the words begins with or contains.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. Not caught above means that no earlier shape of the same mark took the occurrence. A shape's container field is not part of its test: no test here looks at the container, and the checker compares the field afterwards.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number, and the source's tables hold no number for a homonym: they give each expression an id and each meaning an id (the columns id and meaning), and an expression with several meanings stands in a row for each. The route store carries neither id; the dictionary store's record keeps the meaning id and the numbers of the two rows in its location field. So two texts under one letters key may be two words for one meaning or words for two meanings, and the route text cannot say which. By the audit, of the 4,773 keys with more than one text (axis: keys), 2,028 are keys whose routes all cite one meaning id and 2,745 are keys whose routes cite two or more (example key ערב, whose 24 routes cite 7 meaning ids).

branches.question: Some rows hold several words for one meaning, with a comma or a slash between them: dam, fence, barrier. In this dictionary every row is one entry of the source on one meaning, so nothing in the row can tell whether a word in such a list means something different from the rest. Today the page cuts at those commas and prints the words as separate readings, and it does not cut at the slashes. Should these signs cut the row? Until you rule the page prints each of these rows whole, at the commas too. This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: The page prints each part between the signs as a reading of its own, as it does today at the commas: the row dam, fence, barrier prints dam, fence and barrier, and the row Elche/Elx prints Elche and Elx.
The page prints each row as one reading, as written (dam, fence, barrier; Elche/Elx). At the commas this is a change from today.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the store every route that holds no mark, because a shape stands only at a mark («rooster 雌鶏 hen» holds two English words with no sign between them), and every question of whether a row with plain marks renders its Hebrew word; the rows it names for these two questions stand in rows-for-the-store-v1.jsonl, outside the shapes, as examples and no census, and nothing is struck. It leaves to the page the steps that the answers no_pill and word_alone ask for, since a declaration can cut a row and has no field that leaves a whole row out or prints part of a text.
